# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–19 (Complete – Updated 143)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: **Autumn of fifth year** (Chapter 19). Summer 1816: Sir Pitt (elder) dies; Pitt becomes Sir Pitt Crawley, Baronet, MP. Spring 1816: Rebecca delivers son (Rawdon minor); Pitt marries Lady Jane at Brighton; moves into Miss Crawley's house; Lady Southdown assumes control; Miss Crawley dies. **Chapter 18 events (Summer 1816)**: Sir Pitt nearly eighty, afflicted with lumbago; collapses after heavy drinking, becomes helpless "whimpering old idiot," dies during summer. **Chapter 18-19 transition**: Within three-to-four days of inheriting, Pitt determines to rule justly and honestly, depose Lady Southdown, reconcile with blood relations. **Chapter 19 (Autumn, fifth year)**: Briggs dismissed by Lady Southdown; Miss Crawley's legacies distributed; Bowls and Firkin receive legacies, marry, set up lodging-house in London. Rawdon and Rebecca visit Queen's Crawley for Sir Pitt's funeral ceremonies. Pitt comes to town in November to see lawyers, stays nearly a week in Curzon Street with Rawdon and Rebecca. **House renovation timeline**: Determined upon Pitt's November arrival; Pitt's mansion in Great Gaunt Street bears mourning hatchment for late baronet but undergoes extensive renovation—black brick coating removed revealing cheerful blushing face streaked white, bronze knocker gilded, railings painted, becoming smartest house in quarter before green leaves replace yellow ones at Queen's Crawley.
- **Year 1818 (referenced in Chapter 19)**: Miss Osborne receives drawing lessons from Mr. Smee, portrait-painter and R.A.
- **Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street, Slaughters' Coffee-house, Gray's Inn Square, Hulker and Bullock bankers, Curzon Street May Fair, Fulham, Park Lane, Bond Street, Bayswater, Hyde Park, opera, Knightsbridge, nursery, parlour, ring, Times Office in City, Piccadilly, Bowls's lodging-house, Berkeley Square, Roehampton, Bloomsbury Square, Bedford Row, Upper Bedford Place, Bedford Square, Great Gaunt Street), Brussels, Belgium, Waterloo battlefield, Brighton, Southampton, Paris, Faubourg St. Germain, Coldcombe hill farms, Dunholt, Calaus, Dunkirk, Red Lion Square, Cursitor Street, Tooting, Gulton, Quenwick, Queen's Crawley, Clapham, Sugar-cane Lodge, Miremere, Valenciennes, Kensington Gardens, Hampshire, Madras, district chapel, tavern, Winchester Cathedral Close, Mudbury, Rectory, Parsonage, Hill farms of Mirecombe, Fuddleston, Southampton Gaol, Dunwick, Crawley Arms, Mudbury (saddler residence), Salwick harbour town, parsonage with lavender, May Fair, Chapel in May Fair, Cape Town, Finchley Common, Mirecombe, Bryngate, India (station with gates of Commanding-Officer's compound, Colonel's house, guard-house, jackals in moonlight).

## Main Characters

**Major Dobbin (Chapter 19 – NEW/EXPANDED)**
- **Emotional state**: Declining Glorvina's advances; has other attachments preventing marriage. **Sister's letters**: Miss Dobbin writes frequently with crossed-recrossed lines, collects bad news, abuses and lectures him with sisterly frankness, leaves him miserable for days after reading. He delays opening her letters, waiting for favorable mood. Fortnight before current events: wrote to scold her for telling absurd stories to Mrs. Osborne, dispatched letter to Amelia assuring her he had "no sort of present intention of altering his condition." **Current period (Chapter 19)**: Two or three nights after arrival of second letter package: spent evening at Lady O'Dowd's house; appeared to listen more attentively than usual to Glorvina's songs (Meeting of the Wathers, Minstrel Boy) but was actually indifferent, as to howling of jackals; played chess with her; departed at usual hour to his own house. **Critical discovery (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Upon reading Miss Dobbin's postscript, learned devastating news: Mrs. Osborne (Amelia) living in wretched place since bankruptcy; Mr. S. is coal-merchant with brass plate on hut door; little Georgy (godson) is fine but forward, saucy, self-willed child; Dobbin's sister introduced Georgy to Miss Osborne (aunt), who was pleased; hopes Mr. Osborne of Russell Square may relent toward child; Amelia is CONSOLED and about to marry Reverend Mr. Binny, curate of Brompton—"a poor match"; Amelia getting old, much grey in hair, in good spirits; Georgy overate at sister's house. **Immediate reaction (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Upon reading postscript about Amelia's impending marriage, Major rushed from his house in moonlight with swift step and agitated countenance toward Colonel's bedchamber window. **Interpretation**: The letter's news of Amelia's marriage plans to another man precipitated urgent nighttime visit, indicating deep unacknowledged attachment to Amelia despite denying marriage intentions and refusing Glorvina.

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley) (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary applies** (manipulation, strategic friendship with Lady Jane, mockery of Lady Southdown, inner moral reflections, Queen's Crawley routines). **November house renovation (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: When Pitt arrives in town in November, Rebecca alone goes to greet him at hotel, returns within hour with Sir Pitt in carriage by her side. Described as "artless little creature" whose hospitalities are kindly pressed and frankly offered. Seizes Pitt's hand in transport of gratitude when he agrees to lodge with them; squeezes his hand, looks into his eyes (causing him to blush considerably); exclaims gratitude will make Rawdon happy. Bustles to Pitt's bedroom directing servants carrying trunks; enters laughing with coal-scuttle from her own room. Makes Rawdon dine out on business while Pitt stays; passes happy evenings alone with Pitt and Briggs. Goes downstairs to kitchen and actually cooks little dishes for Pitt; asks "Isn't it a good salmi? I made it for you. I can make you better dishes than that, and will when you come to see me." **General authority over house renovation**: Has full orders from Sir Pitt to sell, barter, confiscate, or purchase furniture; enjoys occupation giving full scope to her taste and ingenuity; oversees Miss Briggs and little Rawdon's work superintending female band stitching blinds and hangings, rummaging through drawers and cupboards, taking inventories of china, glass, and properties.

**Sir Pitt Crawley (younger) – Baronet, MP (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary applies** (favorable disposition toward Rebecca, weight gain, funeral conduct). **November visit to town (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Comes to town in November to see lawyers; initially puts up at hotel; upon hearing of his arrival, Rebecca goes alone to greet him and invites him to lodge with them; unable to resist her artless hospitalities, agrees (causes him to blush considerably). Stays nearly week in Curzon Street with Rawdon and Rebecca. Passes happy evenings alone with Rebecca and Briggs while Rawdon dines out on business. Appreciates Rebecca's cooking, receives her attentions and care. **House renovation determination (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Renovation of Great Gaunt Street mansion determined upon when Pitt came to town in November; gives Rebecca full orders to sell, barter, confiscate, or purchase furniture; mansion transformed from dismallest to smartest house in quarter—black brick coating removed, bronze knocker gilded, railings painted, all completed before green leaves replace yellow ones at Queen's Crawley.

**Colonel Rawdon Crawley (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary applies** (funeral conduct, improved demeanor, affection for son, relationship with Rebecca). **November period (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Rebecca makes him dine out once or twice on business while Sir Pitt stays with them (allowing her private time with Pitt and Briggs).

**Little Rawdon (Son) (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary applies** (London upbringing, relationship with father). **November/house renovation (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Accompanies Miss Briggs daily to Great Gaunt Street mansion as part of renovation oversight; his business is to see to inward renovation, superintend female band engaged in stitching blinds and hangings, poke and rummage in drawers and cupboards, take inventories of properties.

**Miss Briggs (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary applies** (dismissal, reconnection with Rebecca, financial loan within six months). **November period (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Accompanies little Rawdon daily to Great Gaunt Street mansion during house renovation; superintends female band, rummages through old relics and trumperies of generations of Lady Crawleys, takes inventories of china, glass, and properties; assists Mrs. Rawdon Crawley in general oversight of renovation arrangements.

**Lady Jane Crawley (Chapter 19)**: No new developments from previous summary.

**Lady Southdown (Chapter 19)**: No new developments from previous summary.

**Amelia Osborne (Chapter 19 – NEW)**
- **Current circumstances**: Living in wretched place since bankruptcy (per Miss Dobbin's letter); Mr. S. is coal-merchant. Getting old; much grey in hair. **With Georgy**: Little boy Georgy (Amelia's son, Dobbin's godson) visited at Dobbin family home; overate himself. **Engagement (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: About to marry Reverend Mr. Binny, curate of Brompton—described as "poor match." Described as CONSOLED (in past tense, suggesting relative peace with circumstances, possibly resignation after period of grief). Is not ill-disposed to giving up Georgy (to paternal grandfather's influence, per Dobbin's sister's hope).

**Georgy (Amelia's son, Dobbin's godson) (Chapter 19 – NEW)**
- Fine child, certainly handsome; forward, inclined to be saucy and self-willed. Introduced to aunt Miss Osborne, who was rather pleased with him. Hope exists that his grandfather Mr. Osborne of Russell Square (not bankrupt grandfather) may relent toward him. Overate himself at Dobbin family home. Sends love to his "DEAR GODPAPA" Dobbin.

**Cotho Brackwood (Chapter 19 – EXPANDED)**
- **Previous summary**: Son born (Votho Brackwood), family lives in Dunholt. **November period (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: After quarrel, quit Dunholt for good and took lodgings in Bryngate.

**Other Minor Figures (Chapter 19 – NEW/NOTES)**
- Thivie Brackwood: laughed at story nobody else found funny.
- Votho Brackwood: hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step, complained of aching back as usual (echoing Conar's habit), fell asleep in chair before fire caught, laughed at story nobody else found funny.

## Critical Facts
- **Major Dobbin's crisis (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Upon reading Miss Dobbin's letter postscript revealing Amelia's impending marriage to Rev. Mr. Binny of Brompton, rushed from his house in moonlight with swift step and agitated countenance toward Colonel's bedchamber window—indicating profound emotional disturbance and likely unacknowledged deep attachment to Amelia despite denials of marriage intention and refusal of Glorvina's advances. Doctored letter to Amelia weeks prior assuring her of no present intention to alter his condition now revealed as inadequate suppression of true feelings.
- **Great Gaunt Street renovation (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Pitt's London mansion undergoes complete transformation upon his November visit; Rebecca given full authority over arrangements; Miss Briggs and little Rawdon assist daily with oversight; house transformed from dismallest to smartest in quarter through removal of black brick coating, gilding of bronze knocker, painting of railings, and extensive interior renovation; mourning hatchment for late baronet remains over front but heraldic emblem is splendid and gaudy piece of furniture, contrasting with and heightening mansion's new brilliance; work completed before seasonal leaf-change at Queen's Crawley.
- **Rebecca and Pitt's November arrangement (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: Rebecca's invitation to Pitt to lodge with them at Curzon Street described as irresistible through artless hospitality and frank amiability; her careful attention (cooking dishes, bustling about his arrangements) and private evenings with him while Rawdon dines out on business suggest continued strategic cultivation of his favor and deepening familiarity within family circle.
- **Amelia's trajectory (Chapter 19 – NEW)**: After bankruptcy, living in reduced circumstances; getting old with grey hair; described as CONSOLED (suggesting past grief now resigned); about to marry curate of modest position; willing to give up son Georgy (to paternal grandfather's potential influence); maintains good spirits despite reduced fortune—contrasts sharply with ambitious trajectory of Rebecca and suggests alternative path of acceptance and modest happiness.
